Description: PDO rules push sheep and goat milk to at least 51% by July 2029; farmers are defending the spec while some cheesemakers want it eased (Cyprus Mail, June 2026). Grocery can list named village and sheep-goat SKUs now, not only cow-heavy supermarket blocks.

Trend: Laiki produce in the dark store
Description: Every town still runs a Saturday laiki that undercuts supermarket fruit by 30-50%. Delivery grocery wins if it copies that quality midweek — especially Nicosia Constanza, Limassol Polemidia, Larnaca and Paralimni — rather than only branded loose veg.

Cyprus Mail's 2026 Nicosia coffee tour (Utu, Kollaborative) plus Limassol roasters Tin and WAGMI and Paphos Beanhaus show roast-at-home is real. List local bags in Limassol Central, Nicosia Central and Paphos; keep it short in Dali and Paralimni.

Pivo (Nicosia, 2015) and Aphrodite's Rock (Tsada/Paphos) are the grocery craft alternatives to mass KEO. Cold-chain cans for Nicosia Central and Paphos; Limassol Central can take a short set. Family stores stay on KEO.

Trend: Geroskipou loukoumi as grocery not souvenir
Description: Loukoumi Geroskipou is Cyprus's first PGI food, still sold mainly as a tourist tin. Aphrodite Delights (1895, Geroskipou) is the listing for the Paphos store, with a smaller gift SKU in Limassol Central — not a default line in Dali or Paralimni.
